title: Why are people saying RIP Fiona? The Cincinnati Zoo hippo died
answer: "RIP Fiona" refers to Fiona the hippo, the Cincinnati Zoo star who became famous after surviving a premature birth in 2017. The zoo announced on Nov. 19, 2026, that she had died at age 9 after swallowing a visitor's knit hat that blocked her digestive system.
body:
Fiona was born at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden in January 2017, about six weeks early and weighing only 29 pounds, far below a typical newborn hippo. Keepers hand-raised her around the clock, and the zoo posted her progress online. Millions of people followed along, and she became one of the best-known zoo animals in the world, with her own web series, books, merchandise and a holiday statue at the zoo. When people post "RIP Fiona," they are mourning that internet celebrity, not a person.

According to the Associated Press, a visitor tossed a knit hat into the air in early November; a ceiling fan caught it and flung it through a small opening above the viewing windows into her habitat. A zoo spokesperson called it an accident. Fiona swallowed the hat, and over roughly 11 days vets sedated her twice for exams, ran an ultrasound and a colonoscopy, and even had her stand on a vibration plate borrowed from a horse farm to help move the obstruction. The zoo said specialists advised that surgery was not an option for a full-grown hippo. On Nov. 19, the zoo said she "did not make it" despite repeated attempts to help her.

The news spread fast because so many people had watched Fiona grow up online, and because it was the same zoo where Harambe, a gorilla, was shot in 2016 after a child got into his enclosure. Fiona's survival had been seen as a turnaround for the zoo after that loss, so many posts link the two. Cincinnati's mayor, the city's pro sports teams and thousands of fans posted tributes, and much of the online anger was aimed at how a stray object could reach an animal's enclosure.

For parents and teachers: children who grew up with Fiona's picture books and videos may be upset. It is also a simple, real-world lesson in why zoos ask visitors never to throw or drop anything near animal habitats.
in_the_news: The Cincinnati Zoo announced Fiona's death on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, and "RIP Fiona" spread across social media the same day.

faq.q: How did Fiona the hippo die?
faq.a: She swallowed a visitor's knit hat that got into her habitat, and it blocked her digestive tract. Vets tried for about 11 days to move it, but she died on Nov. 19, 2026, according to the zoo and AP.

faq.q: How old was Fiona the hippo?
faq.a: Nine. She was born prematurely in January 2017 and would have turned 10 in January 2027.
Harambe was a gorilla at the same Cincinnati Zoo who was shot in 2016 after a child entered his enclosure. Fiona's story was seen as a recovery for the zoo, so people connect the two losses.

faq.q: How long do hippos usually live?
faq.a: Hippos in zoos commonly live 40 years or longer, which is why Fiona's death at 9 shocked fans.
